          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized by
            removing every non-digit character and must contain exactly 10 digits
            afterwards; the stored and returned value is that 10-digit string.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be a
            syntactically valid address. The stored and returned value is normalized
            to lower case.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2026-08-22'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even though another owner
            already has the same last name and address (they share a household).
            Optional; defaults to false. Write-only: it influences creation only
            and is never returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          default: false
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:

        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'

              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1

              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true

              title: Customer code

                upper-cased first three letters of lastName and NNNN is a global 4-digit

I implemented the `namesakeCount` feature: on owner creation, the API now records the number of existing owners sharing the same first name and last name (case-insensitively) *before* this create, and returns it on subsequent reads.

Changes:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — Added a read-only `namesakeCount` (int32, min 0) property to the `Owner` schema, which regenerates `OwnerDto` with the field (MapStruct auto-maps it from the model getter).

3. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — Before persisting, sets `namesakeCount` via a new `countNamesakes(firstName, lastName)` helper that counts existing owners matching both names using the existing `normalizeForComparison` (trim + collapse whitespace + lowercase), so the comparison is case-insensitive and the not-yet-saved owner is excluded.

4. **Schema DDL** — Added `namesake_count INTEGER` to all four `owners` tables (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres); hsqldb is what the tests use.

The new `Cp13Tests.coreCountsNamesakes` passes (two owners named "Ann Sur…" → the second reads back `namesakeCount = 1`), and all pre-existing acceptance tests remain green.
